issues.detail: Hebrew 'בִּדְמִי יָמַי' means 'in the quiet/cessation of my days' (i.e., in the prime/quiet of my life), but Vietnamese renders 'Trong yên lặng đời tôi' which is acceptable; however, the key issue is 'פֻּקַּדְתִּי' — Hebrew is a Niphal perfect meaning 'I have been visited/accounted' (i.e., 'I am deprived/visited upon'), but Vietnamese 'bị lấy đi mất' means 'was taken away', which changes the sense from being 'visited/accounted' (deprived) to 'taken away', altering the meaning of the clause.
